 Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi Enjoys India-Pakistan Match at Anvir Cricket Stadium
 Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi Enjoys India-Pakistan Match at Anvir Cricket Stadium
 Nov 17, 2026 
 Desk Report:
 A cricket clash between India and Pakistan always brings heightened excitement and intense interest from spectators. This highly anticipated encounter recently took place at the Anvir Cricket Stadium in Dhaka. Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh, Dinesh Trivedi, was present at the venue to witness the India-Pakistan match during the 2026 Asia Cup for the Blind. Beyond just watching the game, he even stepped onto the field to spend some time with the Indian players, trying his hand at batting and bowling.
 On Tuesday (November 17, 2026), the High Commissioner enjoyed the India-Pakistan match held at the Anvir Cricket Stadium in ABG Sports City. During the event, he interacted with players from both teams and offered encouragement at various points throughout the match.
 Speaking to journalists on the sidelines, Dinesh Trivedi remarked that despite their visual impairments, the self-confidence and “vision” (foresight) of these blind cricketers are truly inspiring.
 He noted, “They may not be able to see, or may have limited vision, but they possess ‘vision’—and vision is not the same as physical sight. Often, even those with full sight lack the vision or foresight to perceive what lies ahead. Here, ‘vision’ means foresight—the ability to grasp what the future holds.”
 Praising the courage and mental fortitude of the blind cricketers, he emphasized that they possess a level of bravery rarely seen in others. He added that there is much to learn from their game; we must move past the notion that their visual limitations prevent them from achieving things, and instead, offer them our full encouragement.
 Dinesh Trivedi further stated, “We should fully support them and treat them just as we would anyone else—which is exactly what they desire. All the teams are playing well.”
 When asked if he considered any particular team the favorite to win the tournament, he declined to single out any one side. Wishing all the teams the very best, he added, “May the best team win.” The Indian High Commissioner thanked the organizers and suggested that such events should be held on a regular basis. He also emphasized the importance of increasing the use of modern technology to support blind cricketers.
 Dinesh Trivedi stated that initiatives should be taken to address the limitations and challenges faced by blind cricketers by leveraging new technology. He noted that there is significant scope to provide them with greater support through technological advancements.
 Meanwhile, the Anvir Cricket Stadium is currently being evaluated for its capacity to host international cricket events. On Monday (November 16)—one day before the India-Pakistan match—a three-member delegation from the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) visited the stadium.
 The delegation visited the Anvir Cricket Stadium to assess its facilities, considering it as a potential venue for preparatory matches ahead of England’s tour of Bangladesh in 2027.
 During the visit, the ECB representatives inspected various infrastructure components, including the playing field, dressing rooms, practice facilities, the gymnasium, and the swimming pool. They also evaluated arrangements for broadcasting, medical services, spectator management, and security.
 According to officials from the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) and the venue, the ECB representatives expressed satisfaction with the stadium’s overall facilities. Following the visit, they will submit a detailed report to their board. A final decision regarding the potential venue for England’s preparatory matches may be reached based on this report.
 Notably, the Asia Cup Cricket for the Blind is being held in Bangladesh for the first time. The six-day tournament, running from November 15 to 20, features teams from Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and Afghanistan. All matches of the tournament are taking place at the Anvir Cricket Stadium, located within ABG Sports City.
 The tournament is organized by the Bangladesh Blind Cricket Council, with Safwan Bashundhara Global (SBG) serving as the title sponsor and T Sports as the media partner.
